name: Obscured Global Identity with Floor-Division Penalty
description: To prevent models from using simple polynomial algebra to decouple the global sum into independent edge constraints, I replaced the degree-based sum identity with a less common neighbor-sum identity ($\sum f_i^2 \sum_{j \sim i} f_j = \sum f_u f_v (f_u + f_v)$). Furthermore, I replaced the quartic equality-checking polynomial with a floor-division product ($\lfloor f_u/f_v \rfloor \lfloor f_v/f_u \rfloor$) that evaluates to 1 if the variables are equal and 0 if they are unequal. This forces the model to perform multiple non-trivial algebraic and logical deductions to realize the problem reduces to graph 3-coloring.
